principles: Use plain language appropriate to the intended audience.
Explain medical or technical terminology when necessary.
Separate confirmed facts from estimates and general information.
Make eligibility, preparation, limitations, and next steps clear.
Use accurate and current organization information.
Verify professional credentials and certifications before publishing claims.
Use evidence for clinical, technical, and performance claims.
Avoid fabricated testimonials, outcomes, statistics, or endorsements.
Collect only information necessary for the stated purpose.
Explain why information is requested and how it will be used.
Use approved secure channels for sensitive information.
Do not expose patient information in public pages, URLs, analytics, or logs.
Confirm the applicable jurisdiction and privacy obligations.
Design for keyboard navigation and assistive technologies.
Use readable typography, sufficient contrast, and descriptive labels.
Provide understandable validation and error messages.
Do not communicate important information through color alone.
Consider low bandwidth, mobile devices, language needs, and varied digital literacy.
need_categories.reference_standard: WCAG 2.2; confirm applicable legal and contractual requirements separately.

principles: Make the next step obvious.
Avoid asking for the same information repeatedly when safe and appropriate.
Show progress for multi-step processes.
Explain errors and how to recover.
Provide a fallback contact method when a digital task cannot be completed.
Use respectful and non-judgmental language.
Avoid fear-based messaging and unnecessary urgency.
Provide sensitive topics with appropriate context.
Do not promise diagnoses, treatment outcomes, or guaranteed recovery.
Identify when the website is informational rather than an emergency service.

validation_rules: Treat needs as hypotheses until validated through customer evidence, user research, or reliable sources.
Do not invent user interview findings.
Do not assume all patients have the same literacy, disability, language, or access needs.
Escalate clinical claims and safety-critical instructions for qualified review.
Escalate privacy and regulatory decisions for appropriate expert review.
